correctness.rationale: The variance root formula follows by twice differentiating \(\log f_X(e^t)\). For a root pair \(re^{\pm i\theta}\), the per-root real contribution is \(q(r,c)=r(2r-(r^2+1)c)/(r^2-2rc+1)^2\), with \(c=\cos\theta\in[-1,0]\). The identity \(q(r,c)=q(r^{-1},c)\) reduces to \(r\ge1\); the exact radial derivative is nonpositive there, and the angular derivative has at most one zero and can only change from positive to negative. Thus the minimum occurs at \((r,c)=(R,-1)\) or \((R,0)\). Summing per-root contributions gives the bound, and the two displayed PGFs have nonnegative coefficients, satisfy all hypotheses, and attain the two branches.

value.rationale: The primary zero-free variance paper explicitly identifies an exponent gap as an open direction. The closed left half-plane is a standard zero geometry, separately treated as the Hurwitz-stable regime in later probability literature. The result closes that regime exactly: it improves the general half-plane-order lower bound from \(R^{-4}n\) to a sharp two-branch constant of order \(R^{-2}n\) for large \(R\), exhibits extremizers, and identifies the exact transition between real-negative and imaginary-boundary zero configurations.
